findings.detail:
Ground-truth grep over `git ls-tree -r 3c80546f --name-only` (the integration HEAD asserted by the agent's brief as the review target) shows 7 items cite test file globs that match ZERO files on disk:

Real tests are `exec_state_dagcbor_roundtrip.rs` + `exec_state_envelope_shape.rs` + `proptest_exec_state_round_trip.rs`. The substance (schema_version: u8 = 1 at exec_state.rs:line) IS round-trip pinned.
  - Item 13 (DeviceAttestationEnvelope): cites `crates/benten-engine/tests/g16_d_*.rs` — NO match. Real test is `device_attestation_envelope_direct.rs` (single file).
  - Item 14 (DeviceAttestation inner record): cites `crates/benten-id/tests/device_attestation_canonical_*.rs` — NO match. Real tests are `device_attestation.rs` (benten-id + napi mirrors).
  - Item 16 (UCAN body bytes): cites `crates/benten-id/tests/ucan_*.rs` (with trailing underscore) — NO match. Real test is `ucan.rs` (no underscore) + `prop_ucan_attenuation.rs`. The cite to `crates/benten-caps/tests/prop_ucan_window.rs` IS correct.
  - Item 17 (ModuleManifest): cites `crates/benten-engine/tests/g_core_sandbox_*.rs` — NO match. Real tests are `module_install.rs` + `module_manifest_canonical.rs` + `module_manifest_doc_present.rs` + `module_manifest_signature_field_reserved.rs` + `manifest_signing.rs` (5 files in benten-engine/tests/ + an integration/ subset).
  - Item 20 (HandshakeFrame): cites `crates/benten-sync/tests/handshake_*.rs` (with trailing underscore) — NO match. Real test is `handshake.rs` (no underscore).
  - Item 22 (PeerId): cites `crates/benten-id/tests/tf3e_endpoint_id_*.rs` — only partial match (`tf3e_zero_conversion_endpoint_id_is_verifying_key.rs` IS at `crates/benten-sync/tests/` not benten-id; crate-name wrong + glob doesn't match the full name). AND cites `crates/benten-sync/tests/peer_id_*.rs` (with trailing underscore) — NO match; real is `peer_id.rs`.
  - Item 23 (StampedValue): cites `crates/benten-sync/tests/stamped_value_*.rs` — NO match anywhere on tree. The `loro_*.rs` cite IS correct.

Direct impact: a future drift-detector CI lane attempting to walk the inventory + assert presence of named pins via filesystem-glob will return false-positives (the assert exists, but at non-existent files); the §3.6j sweep-completeness self-verify discipline that gates this exact class of drift was applied to inventory STRUCTURE but not to the cite STRINGS. Per HARD RULE 12 + the L11-R3-MAJOR-1 precedent in `b707cb7f` (which closed the IDENTICAL class for items 1+5 in the Summary table 3 hops earlier in this very wave), the phantom-cite class is FIX-NOW.

findings.title: Item 18 PluginManifest 'two distinct CBOR shapes' note correctly named — but only one of the two has its byte-pin test cited
findings.detail: Item 18 names shapes (a) shareable form (with peer_signature) and (b) signing-payload form (without peer_signature; the form the peer signs). Byte-pin cites cover the (a) shareable form (plugin_manifest_full_round_trip.rs + the admin_ui_v0 e2e signature pin). The (b) signing-payload form has its own canonical-bytes shape (it's the prefix the peer Ed25519-signs over); per the §1 'byte-pin test that locks its canonical bytes' framing, BOTH shapes should have a named pin. Grep `signing_payload` or `peer_signed_bytes` at crates/benten-platform-foundation/ shows the production source path; a dedicated round-trip pin asserting the (b) shape is structurally a strict prefix of (a) is the right shape.
findings.fix: OBSERVATION ONLY; not asking for a fix at R6 R2. The current `plugin_manifest_full_round_trip.rs` exercises the encode/verify path which implicitly walks both shapes; a dedicated dual-shape pin is a hardening worth naming in the deferred-row catalog (perhaps as a sub-clause of Row D-9 for the hex-pin G-COMP-1 walk) rather than a R6 R2 fix-now. findings.title: L3-r1-1 binding-message scope-segment uses CBOR-canonical encoding via serde_ipld_dagcbor — RestrictedScope must have deterministic CBOR canonicalization for the binding-sig to be replay-safe
findings.detail: The 5-segment binding-message construction at L97-104 calls `serde_ipld_dagcbor::to_vec(s)` on `Some(s)` where `s: &RestrictedScope`. For the binding-sig to be deterministic across encoders + decoders (a re-verification requirement; one byte diff = BindingMismatch), RestrictedScope's serde impl MUST produce canonical-bytes-stable output (BTreeMap-style sorted-key ordering, no encoder-options drift). serde_ipld_dagcbor is the workspace canonical encoder which IS deterministic by design — verified per benten-core's canonical_bytes_fastpath_stable.rs precedent. So this is structurally correct, but the doc-coupling at RestrictedScope's docstring should explicitly note 'canonical-bytes-stable per the binding-message integrity contract' so a future agent who adds e.g. a HashMap field doesn't quietly break the binding-sig.
findings.fix: Add 1-sentence docstring at `crates/benten-caps/src/restricted_spec.rs` RestrictedScope type: '/// **Canonical-bytes contract:** the serde representation MUST be deterministic + sorted; new fields MUST preserve canonical ordering. Required by `AuthorizationGrant::binding_message` for binding-sig integrity (see L3-r1-1 R6 R1 fix-pass).' Lands at the same R6-FP wave that fixes MAJOR-1.
